standard_prerequisites.name: Regular sections and their zero schemes as effective Cartier divisors
standard_prerequisites.use: Guarantees that the powers s^n are regular sections, which is what makes the comparison of zero schemes valid.

core_obligations: Show that if s is a regular section then so is s^n, that Z(s) -> Z(s^n) is a bijection on underlying topological spaces, and hence that Z(s^n) is disconnected whenever Z(s) is (proof lines 11308-11312).
Consider the canonical short exact sequence 0 -> L^{tensor -n} --s^n--> O_X -> O_{Z(s^n)} -> 0 and the k-algebra R_n = Gamma(X, O_{Z(s^n)}) (proof lines 11312-11317).
If Z(s) is disconnected, deduce that R_n is either zero or contains a nontrivial idempotent, so that Gamma(X, O_X) -> R_n fails to be an isomorphism (proof lines 11318-11323).

Conclude that either H^0(X, L^{tensor -n}) or H^1(X, L^{tensor -n}) is nonzero for infinitely many n, contradicting the vanishing theorems for negative twists of an ample invertible sheaf (proof lines 11324-11328).
proof_roadmap: Compare the vanishing schemes of s and its powers.
Turn a disconnection into a nontrivial idempotent in the sections of the zero scheme.
Extract nonvanishing of H^0 or H^1 of a negative twist on the exact sequence.
Contradict the vanishing theorems for negative twists.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the zero scheme of a regular section s of an ample invertible sheaf on a connected proper scheme whose local rings have depth at least two is connected. The proof argues by contradiction: the vanishing schemes Z(s^n) have the same underlying topological space as Z(s), so a disconnected Z(s) would give a nontrivial idempotent in R_n = Gamma(X, O_{Z(s^n)}), hence the map Gamma(X, O_X) -> R_n is not an isomorphism; reading that off the canonical short exact sequence 0 -> L^{-n} -> O_X -> O_{Z(s^n)} -> 0 forces either H^0(X, L^{-n}) or H^1(X, L^{-n}) to be nonzero for infinitely many n, contradicting the two vanishing theorems for negative twists (proof lines 11308-11328). H3: the idempotent-to-cohomology transfer and the use of both vanishing theorems in one contradiction are independent research-level moves.
